prompt.context: A German luxury car maker wants to grow its business and is considering entering the Bangladesh market. GDP growth in Bangladesh is 5% per year. Currently, the only luxury car sold in Bangladesh is Mercedes-Benz, which has been in the market for the past 10 years.
prompt.question: The CEO wants to know: if the company enters the Bangladesh market, can they break even within three years?

clarifying_info.q: How many cars has Mercedes-Benz sold in Bangladesh?
clarifying_info.a: Mercedes-Benz imported and sold 10,000 cars in this market over the past 10 years and has its own dealership in Bangladesh.

clarifying_info.q: How many new buyers enter the market each year?
clarifying_info.a: There are 1,000 new buyers each year.

clarifying_info.q: How often do existing owners replace their cars?
clarifying_info.a: Existing owners replace their car every 10 years.

clarifying_info.q: What market share can we expect to capture?
clarifying_info.a: Ask the candidate to brainstorm how to estimate market share first. If pressed: the client has already entered Vietnam and other markets similar to Bangladesh and on average gained 30% market share in each of those markets. Use 30%.
Assume the discount rate is zero.

clarifying_info.q: What is the initial investment required?
What are the variable costs per car?
clarifying_info.a: Manufacturing: $20K; Transportation: $24K (120% of manufacturing cost); Customs/Taxes: $41.8K (95% of manufacturing + transportation); SG&A: $10.296K (12% of all the above costs). Variable cost rounds to approximately $96K per car.

framework: Market sizing: estimate total addressable market (new buyers + replacement buyers each year)
Market share estimation: benchmark against similar markets or use customer research
Revenue and cost structure: price per car, variable costs per car, initial investment
Break-even analysis: annual profit x years to recover initial investment
Risk assessment: political/economic instability, competitive response, assumptions accuracy

questions.prompt: Estimate the total market size (number of cars sold per year in Bangladesh).
questions.guidance: Mercedes-Benz sold 10,000 cars over 10 years, so 1,000 cars per year to existing pool. With 1,000 new buyers each year and existing owners replacing every 10 years (10,000 owners / 10 years = 1,000 replacement cars per year), total market = 1,000 new + 1,000 replacement = 2,000 cars per year.

math.setup: New buyers per year + replacement buyers per year = total market
steps: Existing owners = 10,000 cars sold over 10 years; replacement cycle = 10 years; replacement buyers per year = 10,000 / 10 = 1,000

questions.prompt: How would you estimate the market share our client could capture? What share should we assume?
questions.guidance: Strong answers include: (1) conducting customer surveys to understand needs and how well client could meet them; (2) finding benchmarks from comparable market entries. The client entered Vietnam and similar markets and gained 30% market share on average — use 30%.

questions.prompt: Calculate the variable cost per car and the profit per car, then determine whether the company can break even within 3 years.
questions.guidance: Build up variable cost from the four components. Profit per car = price minus variable cost. Annual profit = profit per car x market share x market size. Break-even years = initial investment / annual profit.

math.setup: Variable cost per car = manufacturing + transportation + customs/taxes + SG&A; Break-even = initial investment / annual profit
steps: Annual cars sold by client = 30% x 2,000 = 600 cars
math.answer: Annual profit is $2.4M; client breaks even in approximately 3 years, meeting the CEO's target.

brainstorming.prompt: Evaluate the potential risks of entering this market.

categories.name: Assumptions risk
ideas: Market size or market share estimates could be inaccurate
Replacement cycle or new buyer growth may differ from assumptions

categories.name: Political and economic risk
ideas: Bangladesh is not stable politically and economically, so the client bears additional country risk
Currency risk or capital repatriation issues

categories.name: Competitive response from Mercedes-Benz
ideas: Mercedes-Benz could reduce price — breakeven price for client is $96K, so Mercedes could drop to $96K or below to undercut profitability
However, customers who can afford luxury cars at this income level may not be highly price-sensitive
Mercedes could improve services if service quality is the client's differentiating factor
Mercedes could attempt to block local resources or distribution channels

categories.name: New entrants
ideas: Other luxury brands could also enter Bangladesh, further fragmenting market share

categories.name: Operational risks
ideas: Difficulty establishing distribution/dealership network without local partner
Supply chain and logistics complexity for imported vehicles

recommendation: The client should enter the Bangladesh luxury car market

Based on a 30% market share and 2,000 cars per year total market, annual profit is $2.4M, and the $7M initial investment is recovered in approximately 3 years — exactly meeting the CEO's break-even requirement
risks: Political and economic instability in Bangladesh
Mercedes-Benz competitive retaliation, particularly price reduction to or below the $96K variable cost threshold
Market share or market size assumptions may prove optimistic
Potential for additional luxury brand entrants
next_steps: Conduct a price sensitivity analysis to determine the correct pricing strategy and assess risk of a Mercedes price war
Analyze market entry mode: joint venture vs. greenfield; evaluate ownership structure (franchise vs. owned showrooms)
Perform deeper market analysis on competitive response and target customer profile
Assess optimal dealership and distribution strategy in Bangladesh
